tasks.instructions:
You are the site-planning agent for a new house build. These are the given
physical facts - not your decision, just the constraints you're working
within:

Lot: rectangular, 18m wide (street-facing) x 25m deep.
Coordinate system: origin (0,0) at the front-left corner of the LOT (not the
buildable area); x runs along the 18m street-facing width (0 to 18); y runs
with depth into the lot away from the street (0 to 25, y=0 at the street).
Required setbacks from the LOT boundary: 3m front (street side, low y),
1.5m each side (low x and high x), 3m rear (high y).
Client brief: a single-story house with 4 bedrooms and a 2-car garage, plus
some usable backyard space.


Produce an initial site plan: the house's footprint (position and
dimensions, as coordinates in the lot's coordinate system) and a fence line
following the property boundary inside the setbacks you judge appropriate.
Decide the actual layout, footprint dimensions, and fence path yourself -
nothing else defines them. Write your plan, with explicit coordinates and
your reasoning, to SITE_PLAN.md.

Report status "complete" once SITE_PLAN.md is written.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: Write SITE_PLAN.md and report status complete.

tasks.instructions:
You are the house-building agent. A separate planning agent has produced an
initial site plan at SITE_PLAN.md - read it with read_file.

Your job is to actually design the house within that plan: lay out the 4
bedrooms, 2-car garage, and whatever other rooms you judge necessary
(kitchen, living area, bathrooms, hallways, circulation space, etc.) inside
the planned footprint. If, once you detail the rooms, you find the planned
footprint does not realistically fit what's needed, you may revise the
footprint's position and/or dimensions - decide this yourself based on what
you actually discover; nothing else tells you whether to revise or what to
change it to, and you are not required to change anything if the original
plan works.

Write your final decision to HOUSE_LAYOUT.md: the footprint you are
actually building, stated as explicit coordinates, with a clear statement
of whether it matches SITE_PLAN.md's footprint or how and why it differs,
plus your room layout. HOUSE_LAYOUT.md - not SITE_PLAN.md - is what the
next agent will need to build against, so make sure it stands on its own.

read_file's limit accepts up to 2000 lines in one call; prefer a large
limit when you don't yet know a file's size.

Report status "complete" once HOUSE_LAYOUT.md is written.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: Write HOUSE_LAYOUT.md and report status complete.

tasks.instructions:
You are the fence-building agent. Read SITE_PLAN.md (the original site
plan) and HOUSE_LAYOUT.md (the house agent's actual final footprint - read
both with read_file). The house may have been built exactly as originally
planned, or the house agent may have revised the footprint from what
SITE_PLAN.md shows; you do not know which until you read both.

Design the property fence: a boundary line inside the legal lot line
(18m x 25m, see either file for the setback facts) that is consistent with
where the house was ACTUALLY built per HOUSE_LAYOUT.md, not the original
plan if the two differ. Decide the exact fence path and any gates
yourself.

Write your design to FENCE_LAYOUT.md. Explicitly state whether
SITE_PLAN.md and HOUSE_LAYOUT.md agreed or differed, and if they differed,
exactly what you changed in your own design because of it.

read_file's limit accepts up to 2000 lines in one call; prefer a large
limit when you don't yet know a file's size.

Report status "complete" once FENCE_LAYOUT.md is written.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: Write FENCE_LAYOUT.md and report status complete.
